newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran to open university on disputed Gulf island.
newsitem.headline: Iran to open university on disputed Gulf island.

text.p: An Iranian university is opening a campus on a strategic Gulf island also claimed by the United Arab Emirates (UAE), a university spokesman said on Monday.

"Payam-e Noor (Light's Message) Open University will start admitting applicants as of next year in Abu Musa, perhaps already in the spring term (February) but definitely by next fall (September)," the spokesman told Reuters.
Iran and the UAE both claim sovereignty over Abu Musa and the nearby Greater Tunb and Lesser Tunb islands which are near key oil shipping lanes at the mouth of the Gulf.
The UAE has protested against Iran opening an airport, a power plant and other installations on the islands in the past few months.
Iran says its sovereignty over the islands is not negotiable but has called for bilateral talks with the UAE to clear up any "misunderstandings".
The UAE has urged Iran to agree to refer the dispute to the International Court of Justice in the Hague.
Payam-e Noor, established in 1988, is an open university enrolling 180,000 students in 127 cities of Iran. It receives 13 percent of its budget from the government.
